reference_sql:
SELECT product_id, valid_from, list_price_eur,
       LAST_VALUE(list_price_eur) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY valid_from
                                        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS current_price_eur
FROM price_history
WHERE product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 30
alternatives:
SELECT ph.product_id, ph.valid_from, ph.list_price_eur, cur.list_price_eur AS current_price_eur
FROM price_history ph
JOIN price_history cur
  ON cur.product_id = ph.product_id
 AND cur.valid_from = (SELECT MAX(p2.valid_from) FROM price_history p2 WHERE p2.product_id = ph.product_id)
WHERE ph.product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 30

SELECT product_id, valid_from, list_price_eur,
       FIRST_VALUE(list_price_eur) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY valid_from DESC
                                         ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS current_price_eur
FROM price_history
WHERE product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 30

other_way.sql:
SELECT ph.product_id, ph.valid_from, ph.list_price_eur, cur.list_price_eur AS current_price_eur
FROM price_history ph
JOIN price_history cur
  ON cur.product_id = ph.product_id
 AND cur.valid_from = (SELECT MAX(p2.valid_from) FROM price_history p2 WHERE p2.product_id = ph.product_id)
WHERE ph.product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 30
other_way.tradeoff: Joining the latest version found with MAX works on any engine, but it reads the table twice where LAST_VALUE reads it once.
